turn.user_message: What exactly would our IT team do?
turn.context: From bed-management.md §7.2 (read access) and §7.4.2 (IP extraction, the bill-close and bill-open join, the admissions desk link), with transcript 19 and 20.

transcript.label: After transcript turn 31 · Automations, turn 2 (the record stops at 31)

text: Your IT team gives five things. Four are read access or a report. One is a link at the admissions desk.
bullets: Read access to admissions, discharges and the bed board. Your systems already hold these.
Inpatient notes, pulled out. This lets the engine see who is near the usual stay for their procedure.
One billing report. It sets bill close against bill open on the same bed. That gives dead bed time.
chat.invite: Tell me which systems you run, and I will name the exact asks.
prompts: Why must discharge be built first?
What if some records are on paper?
chat.pointer: Pick an ask to see why it is needed and who in IT does it.
chat.note: Read access and one report. We build everything else.

blocks.title: Five asks, nothing written back
blocks.deck: Each ask is read access or a report. Your teams keep working in the systems they have.

blocks.hint: Pick an ask to see why it is needed and who in IT does it.
blocks.says: These are the five things I would ask your IT team for. Each one only reads. Nothing is written back to your systems.
blocks.label: What I ask your IT team

asks.title: Read access to admissions and discharges
Read access to the bed board
One billing report, bill to bill
A live link at the admissions desk

blocks.park: We bring the rest ourselves: voice notes on rounds, reading OPD prescriptions and timing each admission step. Your IT team does none of these.

sheets.title: Admissions and discharges
sheets.text: The engine reads who came in, who left, which bed and when. It is the record five of the engine’s jobs start from.
sheets.entry: Which system holds admissions and discharges today?

sheets.title: Inpatient notes
sheets.text: The stay so far for each patient. Without it the engine sees only who came and went, not who is near the usual stay.
sheets.entry: Are inpatient notes kept on a system?

sheets.title: The bed board
sheets.text: Which beds are empty, being cleaned or ready. The engine checks it against what the wards say.

lines.label: Used for
lines.value: Checking a bed is really free

sheets.entry: How does your desk see bed status today?

sheets.title: One billing report, bill to bill
sheets.text: Both times already sit in your billing system. The report joins them against the same bed. That gives dead bed time, bed by bed.
sheets.entry: Which billing system do you run?

sheets.title: A live link at the admissions desk
sheets.text: When a planned patient completes formalities, the desk sees a free mapped bed. Once a date is set, it shows on the bed plan with a bed number.

lines.label: Comes
lines.value: After the bed map is built

sheets.entry: How does your admissions desk book a planned patient today?

blocks.label: Written back to your systems
blocks.sub: Every link only reads. Your records stay as they are, and your teams keep working in them.
